scope: Focused primary-source search through 2026-10-17; not an exhaustive novelty review. No cited policy implementation was executed.

sources.title: Learning Fine-Grained Bimanual Manipulation with Low-Cost Hardware
sources.read: Section IV-A and Algorithm 2, plus action representation
sources.supports: Temporal aggregation averages predictions for the same action time with normalized exponential weights. The action representation is absolute joint position.
sources.boundary: Averaging overlapping learned actions is prior art. This scalar target-stream screen does not execute ACT.

sources.title: Real-Time Execution of Action Chunking Flow Policies
sources.read: Abstract, motivation and method scope; existing local report also checked Sections 4.1-4.3
sources.supports: Asynchronous inference keeps a committed action prefix and generates a continuation; naive averaging can combine incompatible action modes.
sources.boundary: Prefix preservation and execution-time reasoning are established. The inspected method is not the proposed robust actuator certificate.

sources.title: Learning Native Continuation for Action Chunking Flow Policies
sources.read: Section IV-D1 stride/ramp ablation and method comparison
sources.supports: More frequent overlap can improve local agreement while degrading whole-trajectory frequency smoothness. Training-time continuation already addresses cross-chunk consistency.
sources.boundary: Local continuity is not sufficient evidence of good global motion or task progress.

sources.title: LiPo: A Lightweight Post-optimization Framework for Smoothing Action Chunks Generated by Learned Policies
sources.read: Sections III-B through III-D and V-A
sources.supports: Combines inference-aware scheduling, overlap blending, jerk-minimizing post-optimization with bounded position perturbations, and quintic interpolation. The discussion explicitly omits robot dynamic constraints to preserve timing and cost.
sources.boundary: Post-processing learned chunks with polynomial smoothing is close prior art. A small joint perturbation or jerk cost is not the proposed closed-loop tracking certificate.

sources.title: VLA-RAIL: A Real-Time Asynchronous Inference Linker for VLA Models and Robots
sources.read: Sections III and IV-C, including temporal alignment and dual-quintic fusion
sources.supports: Models sensor/inference/post-processing timing, fits action trajectories, and uses a chunk fuser intended to retain position, velocity, and acceleration continuity.
sources.boundary: A state-matching chunk fuser is already claimed. Our prior C2 splice certificate is not a new architecture by itself.

sources.title: ChunkFlow: Towards Continuity-Consistent Chunked Policy Learning
sources.read: Sections III-A through III-D, retrieved in-body passages
sources.supports: Uses frozen/editable/future overlap semantics, deterministic blending, seam losses, and history conditioning. Its stated seam-error scaling assumes policy Lipschitz continuity and motion-proportional input drift.
sources.boundary: This is an assumption-dependent seam prediction claim, not a uniform physical jerk or endpoint certificate.

sources.title: World Action Models in Real Time: An Empirical Study of Smooth Execution via Asynchronous Deployment
sources.supports: Compares six execution strategies on a 10 Hz bimanual platform. It reports timing-alignment effects and a precision cost for post-hoc blending, alongside translational RMS jerk.
sources.boundary: The inspected passages do not sufficiently specify signal source and differentiation bandwidth to equate its reported jerk with our modeled physical derivative. Its empirical findings are not independently reproduced here.

sources.title: Execution-Aligned Progressive Noise for Consistent Asynchronous Replanning in Generative Robot Policies
sources.read: Introduction, related work, and persistent-noise formulation
sources.supports: Retains execution-aligned stochastic history across action generation to reduce mode changes beyond the committed prefix.
sources.boundary: Retained internal state in a VLA is not a new general idea. This mechanism is distinct from a deterministic motion reference filter.

sources.title: Recent spline action policies
sources.read: Abstracts and paper structure; not a full proof audit
sources.supports: ABPolicy uses B-spline action representation and asynchronous continuity handling. LieSpline-DP claims cross-chunk C2 continuity through shared boundary control poses on SE(3).
sources.boundary: Do not claim novelty for spline actions, C2 chunk continuation, or Lie-group representation. Full theorem/implementation review remains open.

sources.title: FIR Filters for Online Trajectory Planning with Time- and Frequency-Domain Specifications
sources.version: Biagiotti and Melchiorri; author preprint dated 2012-05-18
sources.read: Abstract, introduction, and Section 2 filter cascade derivation
sources.supports: Derives polynomial trajectories from cascaded finite-memory moving-average filters and treats derivative limits and frequency shaping. More filter stages increase continuity order.
sources.boundary: The four-box method and its smoothness/latency tradeoff are standard FIR trajectory generation. The proposed contribution is the exact history guard and checked composition artifact, not a new filter.

sources.title: Jerk-limited Real-time Trajectory Generation with Arbitrary Target States
sources.version: Berscheid and Kroeger; RSS 2021; maintained repository inspected 2026-10-18
sources.read: Paper scope plus documented current/target state, pass_to_input, input checks, duration and cloud-waypoint caveats
sources.supports: Generates jerk-constrained motion between full position/velocity/acceleration states. It retains generated state through online updates. The community waypoint path can call a cloud service; local point-to-point use is the specified baseline.
sources.boundary: Kinematic jerk constraints and online target replacement are established. Use the real implementation as a baseline. No claims about its physical tracker follow automatically.

sources.title: How to Configure 1kHz Mode
sources.version: Official FANUC ROS 2 driver documentation v2.2.0
sources.supports: The documented mode has controller/option constraints. The page connects host timing jitter to drift or vibration and discusses larger buffers or lower update rates.
sources.boundary: Timing and buffering belong in a practical execution contract. No hardware settings were changed, and this scalar model is not that controller.

sources.title: Explanation of Different Remote-Motion-Control API's
sources.supports: Buffered targets use the native motion planner. Dense target points can affect velocity profiles. Incremental control uses a distinct interpolation-clock contract.
sources.boundary: A native buffered planner is a real industrial baseline; stop-at-each-point control is not a substitute for it.

sources.title: SMOOTH Function Overview
sources.read: Overview and operating notes; earlier frozen local note records response/path tradeoffs
sources.supports: Documents a robot motion filter and conditions on its use.
sources.boundary: Industrial motion filtering exists. This work does not identify a proprietary filter law or reproduce vendor performance.

unresolved: No exhaustive search establishes that the proposed exact knot guard/composition is novel.
No learned-policy code, industrial arm, or contact model was executed.
Besset and Bearee 2017 is a relevant additional FIR baseline in the prior local report; its full PDF fetch failed in this pass, so no new full-text claim depends on it.
